- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >2 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below mean of recent 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 30d), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or 1.5x 30d moving average.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often ignores sentiment and forecasts mean-reversion too aggressively; adjust downward by 3–5% of forecasted range.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 10–15 day smoothing filter to reduce noise.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently underestimates downward momentum in bearish sentiment; add 2–3% buffer to downward forecasts if sentiment < 0.05 for 3 consecutive days.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly rising, model often overestimates upside; cap forecast at 1.1x prior 30d average or 1.2x 14d moving average.
